title: How much more to make one whole?
li: We are learning to find the missing part that makes one whole.
sc: I can find how much more is needed to make one whole
I can use a number line or strip to show my thinking
I can write a number sentence like 3/4 + 1/4 = 1
materials: Make One Whole cards (one set per pair)

slides.title: Warm-up: Wholes and bonds
items: How many quarters in 1 whole and 1 quarter?
slides.notes: Item 3 is a whole number bond on purpose. Today we use the same thinking with eighths.

slides.title: Part, part, whole
slides.intro: A whole can be split into the part we have and the missing part.
slides.notes: Hold up a strip folded into quarters with 3 parts coloured. Ask what is needed to finish the whole before showing the bar.

slides.title: I do: Find the missing part
slides.problem: Ben has 5/8 of a ribbon. How much more to make a whole ribbon?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Find 5/8 on the line: 5 spaces from 0.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.text: Count the spaces on to 1: 6/8, 7/8, 8/8. That is 3 jumps.

slides.notes: Say: I count on from 5/8, the way I count on from 5 to 8. The part size stays eighths the whole time.

slides.title: We do: Missing thirds

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: How many thirds make one whole? (3)

steps.label: Step 2
steps.text: We have 2 thirds. How many more thirds? (1)

slides.notes: Students answer each bracketed question on whiteboards before you reveal.

slides.title: Turn and talk
slides.prompt: Zoe says 3/8 needs 5/8 more to make 1. Ali says it needs 3/5 more. Who is right? Prove it on a number line.
slides.notes: Zoe is right: 5 jumps of 1/8 from 3/8 reach 1. Ali used the 5 jumps but changed the part size, which does not make sense.

slides.title: Which one?
slides.question: What makes one whole with 3/5?
why: Wrong: this child counted the 1 mark between 3/5 and 1 instead of the 2 spaces.
Wrong: this child found 2 but changed the bottom number. The parts are still fifths.
Wrong: this child added the same again. 3/5 + 3/5 is 6/5, more than 1.

slides.title: Show me: missing parts
slides.prompt: Write the missing part on your mini whiteboard.

slides.title: Activity: Make One Whole
steps: Cut out the Make One Whole cards. Lay them face down.
If they make exactly one whole, say the number sentence and keep them.
If not, flip them back. Most pairs wins.
Then do your level on the Make one whole sheet.
slides.notes: Students may use strips to check a pair. Two pairs (1/2 with 2/4, 1/2 with 4/8) also make one whole; accept them if the student can prove it.

slides.support: Lay your part on a strip. Find the pieces that fill the gap to 1, then write the fraction.
slides.core: Find the missing part for quarters, eighths and thirds. Write the number sentence.
slides.extend: Make 1 with 3 parts of eighths, like 1/8 + 3/8 + 4/8. How many ways can you find?

questions: How did the number line help you find the missing part?
Why does the denominator stay the same in 5/8 + 3/8 = 8/8?
slides.connect: We found the missing part to make one whole and wrote number sentences. Which success criteria did you meet?
slides.notes: Add the Make one whole panel to the flip book.

teach.text: Count the spaces from your fraction to 1. 3/4 + 1/4 = 1.

items.q: How much more to make one whole?
How much more to make one whole?
How much more to make one whole?

teach.text: The denominator stays the same. Count on to the whole: 5/8 + 3/8 = 8/8 = 1.

items.q: Mark 3/8 on the line. How many eighths from 3/8 to 1?
Mia has run 2/3 of a lap. What fraction of the lap is left?
Ali says 3/8 needs 3/5 more to make 1. Explain his mistake.
items.answer: The parts are eighths, so the missing part is 5/8. 3/8 + 5/8 = 8/8 = 1.

items.q: A 24 cm ribbon has 3/4 used. What fraction is left? How many cm is that?
Find all the pairs of eighths that make one whole. Start with 1/8 + 7/8.
A path is 30 m long. Sam has painted 2/3 of it. How many metres are left to paint?
Is 1/2 + 3/8 one whole? Explain using eighths.
items.answer: No. 1/2 is 4/8, and 4/8 + 3/8 = 7/8. It needs 1/8 more.

printables.title: Make One Whole cards
printables.instructions: Cut out and shuffle. Lay face down. Flip 2 cards. Keep them if they make exactly one whole and you can say the number sentence.

teacherNotes: This lesson builds part-whole thinking with fractions, the same idea as number bonds to 10. Keep the language 'how many more eighths' so students hold the part size steady. The most common error is changing the denominator (3/8 needs 3/5). The card game has 9 matching pairs; some cards also pair across families (1/2 with 2/4 or 4/8), which is a good talking point for stronger students.
